messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the onboarding RFC — I sketched a small proposal to split the ingest pipeline into two orthogonal surfaces: a lightweight preflight (fast, approximate) and a fidelity bench (slower, thorough).

raj: SGTM. Can you outline the guarantees each surface provides?

maria: Preflight should give binary pass/fail on runtime compatibility (model loads, basic forward, kv cache warm) and a single latency percentile estimate (p95) for canonical prompt set. Target < 120s end-to-end. Fidelity bench runs full eval suite, throughput/cost sweep, quantization smoke, and can take ~30m.

sophie: Important callout: quantization transforms can change tokenization heuristics subtly. Fidelity bench needs to validate decoding parity on golden examples, not just metrics.

ben: Agree. Also we should make the preflight tolerant: a model that fails preflight might still be ok under a different kernel/quant config. Preflight should emit structured signals not hard blocks.

maria: Right — propose preflight outputs: ["load_ok","inference_ok","p95_ms","kv_warm_ok","compat_flags"] where compat_flags is list like ["needs-kernel-fallback","oom-risk"].

raj: How do we avoid duplication between preflight and fidelity bench? Both run similar smoke ops.

maria: Keep preflight scoped to single-shot inference on 3 canonical prompts and one short chat replay. Bench replays wider corpus and long-seq scenarios. Preflight uses cached model artifact; bench may trigger conversions (quantize/opt).

ben: What about interface boundaries? Would teams call both via a single API or separate endpoints?

maria: Prefer separate endpoints to limit SLO expectations. preflight.start(model_id, artifact) -> immediate result object. bench.enqueue(model_id, config) -> async job with logs + metrics URI.

sophie: Async bench should include deterministic artifact IDs for golden outputs so we can diff across commits. Add a checksum field in the bench result.

raj: For rollout gating, we need a compact signal that product teams can evaluate. Maybe bench produces a "gate_passed" boolean and a short reason string.

maria: Yes: gate_passed + evidence_url + regression_score. regression_score is small int where >0 indicates regressions.

ben: Implementation task: add a small validator plugin API so runtime teams can add custom checks (e.g., H100 memory pattern, custom op support). Proposed shape: {"name":"string","run":"command or fn ref","severity":["warn"|"block"],"metadata_url":"string"}.

maria: I like that. CI integration idea: ci-bot runs preflight on PRs for model ingesters and posts quick status to PR. If preflight passes and bench is queued, show a badge "bench: queued".

ci-bot: preflight completed: load_ok=true, inference_ok=true, p95_ms=98, kv_warm_ok=true. bench_job_id=bench_20240305_0912 queued.

raj: Nice. Two engineering questions: 1) sample size and variance for p95 estimate in preflight, 2) who pays compute for bench?

maria: For preflight p95 we sample 100 runs across the three canonical prompts with cold and warm cache mixed (70/30). That gives decent signal without blowing time. For compute billing: bench runs under model-ingest budget by default, but we tag heavy runs to be charged to customer account for private deploys.

sophie: One more tradeoff: strictness of gating. If bench finds a small regression on niche prompt, should we block? We need a tiered policy: critical regressions (e.g., hallucination spike, latency > 2x) block; minor drift creates a ticket and optional rollback.

ben: Agreed. Add a severity taxonomy into bench outputs: CRITICAL / WARNING / INFO. Gate rules map on that.

maria: I'll update the RFC with these interfaces and a short pseudo-API. Also will add a simple JSON schema for the preflight and bench responses. Plan to iterate with runtime and infra next week.

raj: Thanks — can you toss the sample preflight command in the doc?

maria: Pasted sample in thread: 
```
# preflight quick run
redwoodctl preflight --model-id=mdl_1234 --artifact=gs://models/mdl_1234:v2 --prompts=canonical.json --samples=100
```

sophie: LGTM. If you want I can prototype the validator plugin adapter this week.

maria: That would be amazing — thanks Sophie.

ben: I'll scope the bench job metadata and add a minimal UI card for the console.

maria: Cool — tagging follow-ups: @sophie -> validator adapter prototype; @ben -> bench metadata + UI; @raj -> rollout mapping doc. We'll sync Tue. :calendar:

ci-bot: bench_job bench_20240305_0912 started on fleet-dev-3.
